usual_baseline: Clinical Frailty Scale is rarely recorded at first contact in emergency surgery: 0–8% in five audits, 28% in one. Two audits found frailty documented in 65% and 100%. Geriatric or frailty team input is near zero. When scored, 35–43% of older surgical patients are frail. Cognitive screening is poor (AMTS 7%, no cognitive note in 70%).
fix_that_works: Mandatory CFS in software plus poster and teaching: criterion 1 40% to 100% [2197]. Twice-weekly geriatric ward rounds: CFS 0 to 88% [2648]. EPR templates and education: CFS 0/47 to 50%, OPAL review 13% to 34% [2614]. Coloured forms and nurses flagging patients 70+: 0% to 88.2% [2502].
fix_that_fails: Teaching and a screening bundle: CFS 8% to 28%, MUST fell 82% to 67.3% [2784]. Teaching and a frailty section: 2.2% to 18.4% [2566]. Juniors' teaching: memory screen and AMTS fell [2211]. With CFS at 88%, only 18% of frail patients got geriatric input [2648].
consultant_advice: Scoring frailty is well audited and the fix is known: make it mandatory in the clerking system. The gap is what happens next. Measure whether frail patients get geriatric review, cognitive screening and a DNACPR discussion.
